intro: Caruso sings “Recitar!… Vesti la giubba”, the recitative and aria that close Act I of Pagliacci, with orchestra. In the recitative Canio cries out that he is expected to act, and in the aria he orders himself to laugh.

sections.label: A · Canio’s recitative “Recitar!”
sections.mNote: Canio, a husband, faces the performance still to come.

sections.label: C · The clown’s lament
sections.mNote: The aria sets grief as a series of commands to perform.

cues.title: Recitative, “Recitar!”
cues.text: Canio’s recitative comes before the aria. He can scarcely grasp what he is saying or doing, yet the performance must go on. His first word, “Recitar!”, means “To act!”
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo, Pagliacci (1892), Act I, “Recitar! Mentre preso dal delirio”; translation from the Italian libretto. The Victor 88061 attribution supplies the 17 March 1907 date; the transferred disc’s matrix remains unconfirmed. https://www.opera-arias.com/leoncavallo/pagliacci/vesti-la-giubba/
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: The village audience
cues.text: The villagers have come to see a comedy. Canio’s wife, Nedda, plays Colombina. Canio plays Pagliaccio, the husband who is supposed to make the audience laugh when she betrays him.
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo’s libretto identifies Nedda as Colombina and Canio as Pagliaccio; Act I leads into the village audience’s arrival in Act II. Teatro Regio Torino, pp. 2 and 11–14. https://www.teatroregio.torino.it/sites/default/files/uploads/inline-files/20210807%20-%20Pagliacci%20-%20Libretto.pdf

cues.title: Text of the aria
cues.text: The title means “Put on the costume”. Canio tells himself to whiten his face and turn his sobbing into comedy. The words call for laughter throughout, and the tenor sings a lament.
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo’s text, “Vesti la giubba, e la faccia infarina” and “Tramuta in lazzi lo spasmo ed il pianto”, Pagliacci, Act I. This describes the aria’s subject. https://www.opera-arias.com/leoncavallo/pagliacci/vesti-la-giubba/
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Stage direction, end of Act I
cues.text: Leoncavallo ended the act with Canio walking towards the theatre in tears. He pushes the curtain aside, recoils, hides his face in his hands and goes inside.
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo’s stage direction after Canio’s aria, Pagliacci, Act I; Teatro Regio Torino libretto, p. 12. https://www.teatroregio.torino.it/sites/default/files/uploads/inline-files/20210807%20-%20Pagliacci%20-%20Libretto.pdf
